text: dsh-avatar-chat 为 DSH Web 对话中的用户消息和助手回复添加独立头像，并提供“头像对话”设置页。用户可分别控制双方头像的显示，上传图片或输入图片网址，恢复默认图形，并调整头像尺寸。插件通过页面样式装饰对话行，不替换消息组件；设置保存在浏览器本地。适合希望个性化聊天界面的用户，无需 API 密钥或额外账号。

dsh-avatar-chat adds user and assistant avatars to DSH Web chats. Its settings page offers visibility toggles, image upload or URL selection, reset controls, and a 20–64 px size slider. A stylesheet decorates transcript rows; preferences stay in browser storage. No account or API key is needed.

dsh-avatar-chat 的功能「分别控制头像」：设置页可独立切换用户与助手头像，也能为各侧更换图片或恢复默认。
dsh-avatar-chat 的功能「选择头像图片」：可上传常见图片文件或输入图片网址，插件校验输入后用于对应一侧。
dsh-avatar-chat 的功能「调整头像尺寸」：设置页滑块调整头像大小，范围为 20 到 64 像素。
dsh-avatar-chat 的功能「保存偏好」：头像显示、图片和尺寸偏好写入浏览器本地存储，供后续页面读取。
dsh-avatar-chat 使用前须知：头像偏好保存在当前浏览器 localStorage；存储不可用时设置只在当前页面内存中有效。

dsh-avatar-chat README · Introduction：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

dsh-avatar-chat README · dsh-avatar-chat：Dual avatars for the DeepSeek Harness chat transcript — a user avatar on the right of every user turn, an assistant avatar on the left of every answer — plus an **Avatars** page in Settings to switch each side on or off, set a picture, and pick the size.

A DSH Web Client plugin: a Cordis bundle that registers one `settings.section` seat and decorates the transcript with a page-level stylesheet.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Quick start：Three ways in, easiest first. **Plugin market** — switch on **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins → Custom plugin markets**, add this source under **Discover**, and install the card:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/suwodhcbbc/dsh-avatar-chat/main/index.json
```

**One command** — quit the app first, then:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:suwodhcbbc/dsh-avatar-chat
```
dsh-avatar-chat README · Quick start：**From the app** — **Plugins → Add plugin** in the sidebar, same spec. Restart DeepSeek Harness either way. Details in [Install](#install).

dsh-avatar-chat README · Screenshots：Transcript — the user's picture beside the request on the right, the assistant's beside the reply on the left, both at 50 px:

Settings — the **Avatars** page this plugin adds, with a picture chosen on each side:

Both come from the author's own desktop build (Chinese locale, custom wallpaper); the pictures, the size, and the toggles are exactly the controls the page exposes.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Features：- **Two independent avatars.** The user side and the assistant side each have their own visibility toggle, their own picture, and their own restore-to-default.
- **Pictures from disk or from a URL.** Upload PNG / JPEG / WebP / GIF (max 5 MiB, downscaled to 256 px), or paste an `https://…` address. The address is probed once before it is adopted.
- **Built-in look with no picture at all.** With no upload, each side draws a pure-CSS disc using theme tokens only — no bundled image, no literal colour, correct in light and dark.
- **Size from 20 px to 64 px**, applied live to both the transcript and the settings preview.
- **Undecorated where it should be.** One assistant reply is split into a reasoning row and a response row; only the answer row carries an avatar, so a reply never shows two.
- **Clean unload.** Every root attribute and custom property the plugin writes is removed when the plugin is disposed.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-alpha.4` (Web / Desktop). The plugin uses only the shipped theme tokens and the `settings.section` slot.
- The four modules the bundle requires at runtime — `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-store`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` — are all part of the shell's frozen module table, so nothing extra needs installing next to this package.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Install：A profile-local plugin joins a profile as a **bundle**: its `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and the profile lists the package name in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` is *id-targeted* — it can only override or disable an entry a bundle layer already declared — so adding a row there installs nothing.

dsh-avatar-chat README · From the plugin market：DSH ships a custom plugin market. Switch it on — **Plugins → More → Experimental plugins → Custom plugin markets**, then **Plugins → Discover** — add this index source, and the plugin appears as a card you install with one click:

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/suwodhcbbc/dsh-avatar-chat/main/index.json
```

The index pins one exact commit, so a card install is reproducible rather than "whatever `main` is today". Switch the source back off at any time; the plugin stays installed.

dsh-avatar-chat README · From the app：In the sidebar, **Plugins → Add plugin**. Paste the spec, install, then restart:

```
github:suwodhcbbc/dsh-avatar-chat
```

dsh-avatar-chat README · From the CLI：Quit the app first: the `desktop` profile is locked while the application runs.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:suwodhcbbc/dsh-avatar-chat
```

`dsh plugin` forwards the rest of the line to pnpm inside the profile directory, so every spec pnpm accepts works here — `github:<owner>/<repo>`, a git URL, an absolute path (bare or `link:`/`file:`), a `.tgz` URL, or a registry name. Two things happen and there is no third step:

dsh-avatar-chat README · From the CLI：1. pnpm installs the dependency into the profile.
2. Because the package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` gains its name automatically.

Name the profile you actually run: `desktop` for the desktop application, `web` for `dsh web`. Restart afterwards — the bundle stack is composed at boot.

dsh-avatar-chat README · From the CLI：A git-hosted install runs the package's `prepare` script, which pnpm blocks until the exact key it prints is allowed under `allowBuilds`. This package declares no scripts at all, so there is nothing to allow.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Manual install：When pnpm cannot run, the same two facts can be applied by hand: copy `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` and `lib/` into `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-avatar-chat/` (for example `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop`), add `"dsh-avatar-chat"` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and restart. Being listed in `bundles` is what composes the plugin into the tree; it does not also have to appear in `dependencies`.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Verify：After the restart, this should name the package and a real directory:

```
cordis_inspect → host / Config / listConfigs { "entry": "include:ui-avatar-chat" }
```

dsh-avatar-chat README · Usage：Open **Settings → Avatars**.

- **User avatar** / **Assistant avatar** — the switch hides that side from the transcript; the picture button opens a file picker; **Restore default** returns the side to the built-in disc.
- **Picture address** — paste an `https://…` URL and apply it.
- **Avatar size** — 20 px to 64 px. Changes apply immediately.

Nothing else to do: the transcript picks the settings up on the next paint.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Storage and privacy：Preferences live in the browser's `localStorage` under the single key `dsh.avatar-chat.v1`, as JSON:

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1, "size": 28,
  "user":      { "visible": true, "image": "data:image/webp;base64,…" },
  "assistant": { "visible": true, "image": null } }
```

dsh-avatar-chat README · Storage and privacy：- Uploaded pictures are stored as **data URLs** — they never leave the browser, and they are never written into the session log.
- The value is **plain text in origin-shared storage**: any script on the same origin can read it. Do not upload anything you would not put in a local file.
- Reads and writes are individually guarded. A denied origin, an exhausted quota, or a damaged value degrades to in-memory preferences plus an on-page notice instead of breaking the plugin load.
- A document with a foreign `schemaVersion`, an out-of-range size, or a malformed side is repaired in place and reported as damaged.

dsh-avatar-chat README · How it works：DSH has no slot that adds leading or trailing chrome to an individual chat message row: `conversation.chat.node`'s keyed seats are already fully occupied by the shipped renderers (`user`, `steering`, `assistant-step`, …) and a third-party package cannot import or wrap them. Every class name inside the chat subtree is also a CSS-Modules hash, so it is not addressable from another package.

dsh-avatar-chat README · How it works：What *is* stable is the row element itself, which carries `data-chat-flow-kind` (equal to the chat node kind), `data-chat-turn`, and `data-chat-group-part`. So the plugin ships a page-level stylesheet that selects on those attributes, and drives it entirely from root-element state:

- attributes `data-dsh-avatar-chat`, `-user`, `-user-image`, `-assistant`, `-assistant-image`
- custom properties `--dsh-avatar-chat-size` and the two picture variables

dsh-avatar-chat README · How it works：The avatar is painted by an absolutely-positioned `::before` inside padding the stylesheet reserves on the decorated row; the row keeps its shipped `display`, so host layout is untouched.

The stylesheet is a plain `.css` side-effect import, which the DSH client bundler turns into a tagged `<style data-plugin-css>` element — deduplicated by tag id, so re-running the plugin never double-injects it. Every root write is absolute, so applying twice is idempotent.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Known limitations：- The decoration depends on `data-chat-flow-kind`, which is **not a published contract**. If the chat row markup changes, avatars disappear silently until the selector is updated.
- Only `user`, `steering` and `assistant-step` rows are decorated. Tool calls, commands, system prompts and turn-process rows have no avatar.
- A decorated row becomes `position: relative`, so it is the containing block for its own absolutely-positioned descendants.
- The avatar carries no per-message identity — there is exactly one user picture and one assistant picture at a time.
- A remote picture address is probed once when it is applied and is not revalidated afterwards.
- The built-in disc uses `--dsw-alias-brand-primary`, which is near-black in light mode and near-white in dark mode — an inverse monochrome accent, not a brand blue.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Compatibility：Verified against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-alpha.4` on Windows with the shipped Web client, in both unit tests and a real headless-Chromium run against an assembled profile.

dsh-avatar-chat README · Building from source：The `lib/` directory in this repository is the built artifact and is what the loader consumes. Rebuilding it requires a DeepSeek Harness source checkout: this package is compiled by the repository's shared client bundler preset (`packages/client/tsdown.client.ts`), which owns the `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` wrapper, the platform externals, and the CSS inlining.

To rebuild: place `src/` at `packages/client/ui-avatar-chat/src` in the checkout, then

dsh-avatar-chat README · Building from source：```sh
pnpm --filter @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-avatar-chat bundle
```

Keep the package name in sync — the module id baked into `lib/client.js` comes from `package.json`, and the loader matches the bundle row to that id.
